target_customer: Adults with insulin treated diabetes and the clinicians who manage them; patients used it free and providers were the economic buyer
problem: Patients adjusted insulin only at infrequent clinic visits, using paper logs and nurse phone calls. DoseDr let patients log glucose and injections, suggested regimen changes and let providers adjust doses remotely.
business_model: Free patient app with a provider web portal; revenue model not stated in sources found
product_category: Digital health insulin dosing and remote care

founders.name: John Sanders
founders.background_notes: Only founder named on the YC page. No background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile app plus provider portal was ordinary engineering, but safe dose recommendations and clinical workflow integration are harder and carry medical device regulatory risk.

defensibility.rationale: Dose logging apps were common and a provider network was the only possible moat, which a 2 person team had not built.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large pharma and digital health firms later received FDA clearance for their own insulin dosing apps (MobiHealthNews reports on Sanofi and Eli Lilly clearances, 2017 and later). DoseDr's outcome is not documented.

market_need_then: YC's launch post (2016-03) said existing apps tracked data without helping doctors adjust treatment in real time and the alternatives were paper logs, clinic visits and nurse calls. It was live in California and Louisiana.

branding.domain_note: dosedr.com redirected to a domain reseller listing when fetched in 2026; a secondary directory says the last working homepage capture was 2019.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, community or merch was found; search results were dominated by similarly named dosing apps.

outcome_analysis: DoseDr graduated from YC in Winter 2016 with a two person team and a free insulin dosing app aimed at remote clinician adjustment. The cause of its inactive status is not public: no shutdown post, press or founder statement was found, so no failure factors are recorded. Pharma backed dosing apps cleared by the FDA after 2016 show a regulated space where a small team faced strong incumbents.
notes: Cause of inactivity is not public. The seed entry rests on a single database (Wellfound lists Seed, Mar 2016, no amount) and may only reflect the standard YC deal; a second profile estimates total funding under $1M and Crunchbase lists a second founder, Marlon Castillo, which no opened source confirms so he is not listed. One aggregator claims a 2018 expansion to hypertension; unverified. No competitor with a source dated near the batch was opened (a mySugr article was blocked), so the list is empty. Company site was a parked domain, so the site note is a dead site.
